question: How many customers are in the USA?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS TotalCustomers FROM "Customer" WHERE "Country" = 'USA'

question: List all customers from Canada ordered by last name
sql: SELECT "FirstName", "LastName", "City" FROM "Customer" WHERE "Country" = 'Canada' ORDER BY "LastName" ASC

question: Get total invoices and total sales amount per customer
sql: SELECT c."CustomerId", c."FirstName", c."LastName", COUNT(i."InvoiceId") AS TotalInvoices, COALESCE(SUM(i."Total"), 0) AS TotalSpent FROM "Customer" AS c LEFT JOIN "Invoice" AS i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId" GROUP BY c."CustomerId", c."FirstName", c."LastName"

question: Find the top 5 customers by total spending
sql: SELECT c."CustomerId", c."FirstName", c."LastName", SUM(i."Total") AS TotalSpent FROM "Customer" AS c JOIN "Invoice" AS i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId" GROUP BY c."CustomerId", c."FirstName", c."LastName" ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 5

question: Count how many tracks exist in each genre
sql: SELECT g."Name" AS Genre, COUNT(t."TrackId") AS TrackCount FROM "Genre" AS g LEFT JOIN "Track" AS t ON g."GenreId" = t."GenreId" GROUP BY g."Name" ORDER BY TrackCount DESC

question: Get album titles with their artist names
sql: SELECT al."Title" AS AlbumTitle, ar."Name" AS ArtistName FROM "Album" AS al JOIN "Artist" AS ar ON al."ArtistId" = ar."ArtistId" ORDER BY ar."Name", al."Title"

question: Find employees who report to the General Manager
sql: SELECT e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName", e."LastName" FROM "Employee" AS e WHERE e."ReportsTo" = (SELECT "EmployeeId" FROM "Employee" WHERE "Title" = 'General Manager')

question: Which country generated the highest revenue?
sql: SELECT "BillingCountry", SUM("Total") AS Revenue FROM "Invoice" GROUP BY "BillingCountry" ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1

question: List customers who never made a purchase
sql: SELECT c."CustomerId", c."FirstName", c."LastName" FROM "Customer" AS c LEFT JOIN "Invoice" AS i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId" WHERE i."InvoiceId" IS NULL

question: Get the most purchased track
sql: SELECT t."Name", SUM(il."Quantity") AS TotalPurchased FROM "InvoiceLine" AS il JOIN "Track" AS t ON il."TrackId" = t."TrackId" GROUP BY t."TrackId", t."Name" ORDER BY TotalPurchased DESC LIMIT 1

question: Find total sales per employee support representative
sql: SELECT e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName", e."LastName", SUM(i."Total") AS TotalSales FROM "Employee" AS e JOIN "Customer" AS c ON e."EmployeeId" = c."SupportRepId" JOIN "Invoice" AS i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId" GROUP BY e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName", e."LastName" ORDER BY TotalSales DESC

question: Get monthly revenue for 2024
sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', "InvoiceDate") AS Month, SUM("Total") AS Revenue FROM "Invoice" WHERE strftime('%Y', "InvoiceDate") = '2024' GROUP BY Month ORDER BY Month

question: Find the longest track in each album
sql: SELECT AlbumTitle, TrackName, Duration FROM (SELECT al."Title" AS AlbumTitle, t."Name" AS TrackName, t."Milliseconds" AS Duration, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t."AlbumId" ORDER BY t."Milliseconds" DESC, t."TrackId") AS TrackRank FROM "Track" AS t JOIN "Album" AS al ON t."AlbumId" = al."AlbumId") AS ranked WHERE TrackRank = 1 ORDER BY Duration DESC

question: Which customers spent more than the average customer spending?
sql: SELECT c."CustomerId", c."FirstName", c."LastName", SUM(i."Total") AS TotalSpent FROM "Customer" AS c JOIN "Invoice" AS i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId" GROUP BY c."CustomerId", c."FirstName", c."LastName" HAVING SUM(i."Total") > (SELECT AVG(CustomerTotal) FROM (SELECT SUM("Total") AS CustomerTotal FROM "Invoice" GROUP BY "CustomerId") AS customer_totals)

question: Rank customers by spending within each country
sql: SELECT "BillingCountry", "CustomerId", TotalSpent, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY "BillingCountry" ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC) AS CountryRank FROM (SELECT c."CustomerId", i."BillingCountry", SUM(i."Total") AS TotalSpent FROM "Customer" AS c JOIN "Invoice" AS i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId" GROUP BY c."CustomerId", i."BillingCountry") AS totals

question: List all employees with the names of the managers they report to
sql: SELECT e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName" || ' ' || e."LastName" AS EmployeeName, m."FirstName" || ' ' || m."LastName" AS ManagerName FROM "Employee" AS e LEFT JOIN "Employee" AS m ON e."ReportsTo" = m."EmployeeId" ORDER BY ManagerName

question: Find employees who do not report to anyone
sql: SELECT "EmployeeId", "FirstName", "LastName", "Title" FROM "Employee" WHERE "ReportsTo" IS NULL

question: Get the direct subordinates of the General Manager
sql: SELECT e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName", e."LastName" FROM "Employee" AS e WHERE e."ReportsTo" = (SELECT "EmployeeId" FROM "Employee" WHERE "Title" = 'General Manager')

question: List employees along with their manager and their manager's manager
sql: SELECT e."FirstName" || ' ' || e."LastName" AS EmployeeName, m."FirstName" || ' ' || m."LastName" AS ManagerName, mm."FirstName" || ' ' || mm."LastName" AS SeniorManagerName FROM "Employee" AS e LEFT JOIN "Employee" AS m ON e."ReportsTo" = m."EmployeeId" LEFT JOIN "Employee" AS mm ON m."ReportsTo" = mm."EmployeeId"

question: Find the hierarchy depth for each employee
sql: WITH RECURSIVE EmployeeHierarchy AS (SELECT "EmployeeId", "FirstName", "LastName", "ReportsTo", 0 AS Level FROM "Employee" WHERE "ReportsTo" IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName", e."LastName", e."ReportsTo", eh.Level + 1 FROM "Employee" AS e JOIN EmployeeHierarchy AS eh ON e."ReportsTo" = eh."EmployeeId") SELECT "EmployeeId", "FirstName", "LastName", Level FROM EmployeeHierarchy ORDER BY Level, "EmployeeId"

question: Count how many employees report under each manager
sql: SELECT m."EmployeeId", m."FirstName" || ' ' || m."LastName" AS ManagerName, COUNT(e."EmployeeId") AS DirectReports FROM "Employee" AS m LEFT JOIN "Employee" AS e ON e."ReportsTo" = m."EmployeeId" GROUP BY m."EmployeeId", m."FirstName", m."LastName" ORDER BY DirectReports DESC

question: Find managers who have more than two direct reports
sql: SELECT m."EmployeeId", m."FirstName", m."LastName", COUNT(e."EmployeeId") AS DirectReports FROM "Employee" AS m JOIN "Employee" AS e ON e."ReportsTo" = m."EmployeeId" GROUP BY m."EmployeeId", m."FirstName", m."LastName" HAVING COUNT(e."EmployeeId") > 2

question: List the full reporting chain for employee 5
sql: WITH RECURSIVE ReportingChain AS (SELECT "EmployeeId", "FirstName", "LastName", "ReportsTo" FROM "Employee" WHERE "EmployeeId" = 5 UNION ALL SELECT e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName", e."LastName", e."ReportsTo" FROM "Employee" AS e JOIN ReportingChain AS rc ON rc."ReportsTo" = e."EmployeeId") SELECT * FROM ReportingChain

question: Find all employees under the General Manager at every hierarchy level
sql: WITH RECURSIVE OrgTree AS (SELECT "EmployeeId", "FirstName", "LastName", "ReportsTo" FROM "Employee" WHERE "Title" = 'General Manager' UNION ALL SELECT e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName", e."LastName", e."ReportsTo" FROM "Employee" AS e JOIN OrgTree AS ot ON e."ReportsTo" = ot."EmployeeId") SELECT * FROM OrgTree WHERE "EmployeeId" != (SELECT "EmployeeId" FROM "Employee" WHERE "Title" = 'General Manager')

question: Calculate total sales generated by each manager's entire team
sql: WITH RECURSIVE TeamHierarchy AS (SELECT "EmployeeId", "ReportsTo" FROM "Employee" UNION ALL SELECT e."EmployeeId", th."ReportsTo" FROM "Employee" AS e JOIN TeamHierarchy AS th ON e."ReportsTo" = th."EmployeeId"), TeamSales AS (SELECT th."ReportsTo" AS ManagerId, SUM(i."Total") AS TeamRevenue FROM TeamHierarchy AS th JOIN "Customer" AS c ON th."EmployeeId" = c."SupportRepId" JOIN "Invoice" AS i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId" GROUP BY th."ReportsTo") SELECT e."EmployeeId", e."FirstName", e."LastName", ts.TeamRevenue FROM "Employee" AS e LEFT JOIN TeamSales AS ts ON e."EmployeeId" = ts.ManagerId ORDER BY ts.TeamRevenue DESC
